about.title: Porterville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Porterville's traffic pattern tells its own story: public records show 246 injury collisions and 355 people hurt in the most recent final year, with Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest concentration of reported crashes. Corridors like Olive Avenue, Henderson Avenue, Main Street, and Morton Avenue see a steady share of that volume. Whether you were rear-ended near a busy intersection or caught in a multi-car collision during Friday rush hour, the days right after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters move quickly, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Porterville residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid common missteps with insurers. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: Your Timeline Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which clock applies before it runs out.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame the insurer assigns you. What you say in an early recorded statement can be used to inflate that percentage, so it helps to have guidance before speaking with any adjuster.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but insurers still negotiate hard against those claims. An attorney working on contingency only gets paid if you recover, so there's no upfront cost to have someone advocate for the full value of your losses.

items.question: I was in a crash near Henderson Avenue during rush hour — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if you feel okay, since some injuries surface hours or days later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for any witnesses, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've spoken with an independent attorney. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles Porterville-area crashes at no cost to you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Porterville car accident?
items.answer: Generally, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned vehicle or road, such as a city or county vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months. Because these timelines vary, it's worth confirming which applies to your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the other driver says the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partially responsible, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. This makes it especially important not to speculate about fault in conversations with insurers. An independent attorney can help you understand how fault might be allocated based on the facts of your Porterville crash.
